drivingQuestion: What is the scriptural source that one stands to pray only from gravity (כובד ראש)?
outcomeNote: Three proposed sources (Hannah, David's entry, בהדרת קדש) are rejected; Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak's עבדו את ה׳ ביראה וגילו ברעדה stands, and the sugya turns to rejoicing with trembling

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״וְהִיא מָרַת נָפֶשׁ״.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» We learned in the mishna that prayer should be undertaken in an atmosphere of gravity. The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? Rabbi Elazar said: They are derived from the verses describing the prayer of Hannah, mother of Samuel, «as the verse states: “And she felt bitterness of soul,» and she prayed to the Lord and she wept and wept” (I Samuel 1:10).

segments.he: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא חַנָּה שָׁאנֵי, דַּהֲוָת מְרִירָא לִבָּא טוּבָא.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this proof: «From what» does that conclusion ensue? «Perhaps Hannah is different, as» her «heart was extremely embittered,» her prayer was embittered as well. This does not prove that everyone must pray in that frame of mind.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, מֵהָכָא: ״וַאֲנִי בְּרֹב חַסְדְּךָ אָבוֹא בֵיתֶךָ אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה אֶל הֵיכַל קׇדְשְׁךָ בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ״.
segments.en: «Rather, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said,» it can be proved «from here,» as David said: «“But as for me, by Your abundant loving-kindness I will enter Your house, at Your Holy Temple I will bow in reverence for You”» (Psalms 5:8). Entering into prayer like entering the Holy Temple must be performed reverentially.

segments.he: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא דָּוִד שָׁאנֵי, דַּהֲוָה מְצַעַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ בְּרַחֲמֵי טוּבָא. אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, מֵהָכָא: ״הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַה׳ בְּהַדְרַת קֹדֶשׁ״: אַל תִּקְרֵי ״בְּהַדְרַת״ אֶלָּא ״בְּחֶרְדַּת״.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this proof as well: «From what» does that conclusion ensue? «Perhaps David is different, as he would excessively afflict himself in prayer» in order to atone for his transgression with Bathsheba. Consequently, his cannot serve as a paradigm for proper conduct in prayer. «Rather, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said,» it can be derived «from here,» from this verse that David said, not about his own worship, but about worship of God in general: “Give, unto the Lord, the honor of His name, «bow to the Lord in the beauty of holiness [behadrat kodesh]”» (Psalms 29:2). «Do not read: In the beauty of [behadrat]» holiness. «Rather» read: «In trembling of [beḥerdat]» holiness; one must enter into prayer from an atmosphere of gravity engendered by sanctity.

segments.he: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לְךָ, ״הַדְרַת״ מַמָּשׁ. כִּי הָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה הֲוָה מְצַיֵּין נַפְשֵׁיהּ, וַהֲדַר מְצַלֵּי. אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מֵהָכָא: ״עִבְדוּ אֶת ה׳ בְּיִרְאָה וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה״.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this too: «From what» does that conclusion ensue? «Perhaps, actually I would say to you» that it should be read as it is written: «Specifically, “in the beauty,”» and it means that one should pray in beautiful clothing, «as» in the case «of Rav Yehuda who would adorn himself and then pray.» Rav Yehuda believed that one who comes before the King must wear his most beautiful clothing. The Gemara has yet to find a source for the halakha that one must approach prayer from an atmosphere of gravity. «Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said» it can be derived «from here,» from this verse: «“Serve the Lord in fear and rejoice with trembling”» (Psalms 2:11).

segments.he: מַאי ״וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה״? אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא אָמַר רַבָּה: בִּמְקוֹם גִּילָה שָׁם תְּהֵא רְעָדָה.
segments.en: Having cited this verse from Psalms, the Gemara asks: «What is» the meaning of «rejoice with trembling? Rav Adda bar Mattana said» that «Rabba said:» One may not experience unbridled joy; even «where there is rejoicing, there should be trembling.»

segments.he: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה חַזְיֵיהּ דַּהֲוָה קָא בָדַח טוּבָא. אֲמַר ״וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה״ כְּתִיב!
segments.en: On that note, the Gemara relates: «Abaye was sitting before» his teacher «Rabba,» and Rabba «saw that he was excessively joyful. He said» to Abaye: «It is written: Rejoice with trembling,» one’s joy should not be unrestrained.
Abaye «said to him:» It is permissible for me because «I am donning phylacteries» now and as long as they are upon me they ensure that the fear of God is upon me.

segments.he: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא. חַזְיֵיהּ דַּהֲוָה קָא בָדַח טוּבָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״בְּכׇל עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר״ כְּתִיב?
segments.en: Similarly, the Gemara relates that «Rabbi Yirmeya was sitting before Rabbi Zeira. He saw that Rabbi Yirmeya was excessively joyful. He said to him: It is written: “In all sorrow there is profit”» (Proverbs 14:23); sorrow is appropriate, not excessive joy.
Rabbi Yirmeya «said to him:» It is permissible for me because «I am donning phylacteries.»

segments.he: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא עֲבַד הִילּוּלָא לִבְרֵיהּ, חֲזַנְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דַּהֲווֹ קָבָדְחִי טוּבָא.
segments.en: On a similar note, the Gemara relates: «Mar, son of Ravina, made a wedding» feast «for his son» and «he saw the Sages, who were excessively joyous.»

segments.he: אַיְּיתִי כָּסָא דְמוֹקְרָא בַּת אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזִי, וְתַבַּר קַמַּיְהוּ, וְאִעֲצִיבוּ.
segments.en: «He brought a valuable cup worth four hundred zuz and broke it before them and they became sad.»

segments.he: רַב אָשֵׁי עֲבַד הִילּוּלָא לִבְרֵיהּ, חֲזַנְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דַּהֲווֹ קָא בָדְחִי טוּבָא. אַיְּיתִי כָּסָא דְּזוּגִּיתָא חִיוָּרְתָּא, וְתַבַּר קַמַּיְהוּ, וְאִעֲצִיבוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara also relates: «Rav Ashi made a wedding» feast «for his son» and «he saw the Sages, who were excessively joyous. He brought a cup of» extremely valuable «white glass and broke it before them, and they became sad.»

segments.he: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא זוּטֵי בְּהִלּוּלָא דְּמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא: לִישְׁרֵי לַן מָר. אֲמַר לְהוּ: וַי לַן, דְּמִיתְנַן. וַי לַן, דְּמִיתְנַן. אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אֲנַן מָה נַעֲנֵי בָּתְרָךְ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: הֵי תּוֹרָה, וְהֵי מִצְוָה דְּמַגְּנוּ עֲלַן.
segments.en: Similarly, the Gemara relates: «The Sages said to Rav Hamnuna Zuti at the wedding» feast «of Mar, son of Ravina: Let the Master sing for us.» Since he believed that the merriment had become excessive, «he said to them,» singing: «Woe unto us, for we shall die, woe unto us, for we shall die. They said to him: What shall we respond after you?» What is the chorus of the song? «He said to them,» you should respond: «Where is Torah and where is mitzva that protect us?»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי: אָסוּר לְאָדָם שֶׁיְּמַלֵּא שְׂחוֹק פִּיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אָז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ וּלְשׁוֹנֵנוּ רִנָּה״. אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁ״יֹּאמְרוּ בַגּוֹיִם הִגְדִּיל ה׳ לַעֲשׂוֹת עִם אֵלֶּה״. אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ שֶׁמִּיָּמָיו לֹא מִלֵּא שְׂחוֹק פִּיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, מִכִּי שַׁמְעַהּ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבֵּיהּ.
segments.en: In a similar vein, «Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: One is forbidden to fill his mouth with mirth in this world,» as long as we are in exile (ge’onim), «as it is stated:» “When the Lord returns the captivity of Zion we will be as dreamers” (Psalms 126:1). Only «“then will our mouths fill with laughter and our lips with song”» (Psalms 126:2). «When» will that joyous era arrive? When «“they will say among nations, the Lord has done great things with these”» (Psalms 126:2). «They said about Reish Lakish that throughout his life he did not fill his mouth with laughter in this world once he heard this» statement «from his teacher, Rabbi Yoḥanan.»

edges.cueHe: אמרו ליה רבנן לרב המנונא זוטי בהלולא דמר בריה דרבינא: לישרי לן מר
edges.about: ask him to sing for them at the wedding feast of Mar son of Ravina

edges.cueHe: בהלולא דמר בריה דרבינא
edges.about: present at the wedding feast Mar son of Ravina made for his son

edges.cueHe: אמר להו: וי לן, דמיתנן
edges.about: sings: woe unto us, for we shall die

edges.cueHe: אמרי ליה: אנן מה נעני בתרך?
edges.about: what refrain they should answer after him

edges.cueHe: אמר להו: הי תורה, והי מצוה דמגנו עלן
edges.about: the refrain: where is Torah and where is mitzva that protect us

edges.cueHe: אמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי שמעון בן יוחאי
edges.about: one is forbidden to fill his mouth with laughter in this world

edges.cueHe: שנאמר
edges.about: then will our mouths fill with laughter — when they say among the nations the Lord has done great things

edges.cueHe: אימתי, בזמן ש
edges.about: the time of full laughter is only when the nations say the Lord has done great things — not in this world

edges.cueHe: אמרו עליו על ריש לקיש
edges.about: Reish Lakish never filled his mouth with laughter in this world once he heard this from R' Yochanan

edges.cueHe: מכי שמעה מרבי יוחנן רביה
edges.about: heard this teaching from R' Yochanan, his teacher
